unresolved: RESOLVED 2026-10-10 (was: 'One status summary per outcome is violated on seven closed outcomes (#50, #63, #67, #75, #86, #88, #90)'). Cleared by repair forward under maintainer authorization on issue #116: nine superseded `## YOLO status` summaries on #50, #63, #67, #75 (x4), #88 and #90 were demoted to dated history with their bodies preserved verbatim and nothing deleted, and #86 - whose summary had been posted into the issue description rather than a comment - received that same already-published text as a status comment, verified line-for-line identical before posting. Every one of the seven outcomes now carries exactly one summary, and a re-run of the pinned alpha.16 validator reports ZERO issue_summary findings, down from seven. The contract .yolo/governance/specs/status-presentation.md was NOT amended and the alternative options (amend the contract, delete the duplicates) were NOT taken. Authorization: recognized maintainer normzhou, in an authenticated harness session, delegated the A/B/C choice to the agent's judgement where it neither involves changing the Charter nor violates it; option A was selected under that delegation. Q3 remains unverified because the `release` finding is still open - see below - but this specific blocker is cleared and the checkpoint is now blocked by the release finding alone.

Release finding, cause identified 2026-10-10 by walking every committed value of verification.release.effective_commit: the sequence is null -> 6efd602 (set when the alpha.11 upgrade landed) -> dbfdacf2 (6e36c17e, 'Record the v0.3.0 release observations') -> 80bf5f86 (c03d2434, 'Record the v0.3.1 release observations') -> back to 6efd602 (f40a1801, the alpha.16 upgrade). The two intermediate values were this repository's OWN bookkeeping error: recording a release observation wrongly re-pointed effective_commit at that release's commit, conflating the fixed applicability boundary with a tag->commit mapping. records.md says 'Preserve an established boundary on upgrade', which is what f40a1801 correctly did. So the CURRENT value 6efd602 is right, the target defect is already repaired, and what remains unsatisfiable is the validator rule requiring the current value to match every published revision - which penalises the target for having corrected itself. That is a rule-design question about upstream yolo-dev, not a defect in this repository. Tracked on issue #116.

RESOLVED 2026-10-11 by the alpha.20 upgrade (PR #124, effective 030b6ca): the release_history recoverable-v1 profile anchors the release boundary at its establishment, so the previously unsatisfiable effective_commit finding clears, the v0.3.2 annotated-tag-object entries in legacy_tags and releases-observed-2026-10-08.json are corrected to the immutable commit 75cfffb, and the dropped 2026-10-06 observation reference is restored. Root cause and both upstream reports retained in .yolo/reports/upgrade-alpha16-proposal.json and issue #116.

Still open after the upgrade: the adoption checkpoint is not advanced (it stays at 31c0f8b) because advancing it requires a review report naming ownership, congruence, verification and continuity with evidence for the whole interval since that commit. That is separate work from the migration, and the alpha.20 pin needs a fresh-session continuation record before any dependent claim is restored. Also live: the e2e/review capture set is not byte-reproducible (13-14 of 34 files change pixels between runs of identical code).
